title: 花 (Hana — Flowers, 春のうらら)
description: A classic Meiji-era art song celebrating spring on the Sumida River in Tokyo. Boats glide up and down the hazy river, and even the drops falling from the oars scatter like cherry blossoms. The melody was composed by 瀧廉太郎 (Taki Rentaro), who died of tuberculosis at age 23 — making this one of Japanese music history's most poignant compositions. First movement of his four-season song cycle '四季.'
